newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees mining exports up to $4.5 bln by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees mining exports up to $4.5 bln by 2000.

text.p: Peru expects to increase its mining exports to between $4 billion and $4.5 billion by 2000, from an estimated $2.8 billion this year, president of Congress' Energy and Mines committee Eduardo Pando said Friday.
Total mining exports in 1996 were $2.609 billion.
"The increase in mining exports is going to contribute enormously to reducing our commercial deficit," Pando said.

Peru's trade deficit more than doubled to $2.115 billion in 1995 from $1.021 billion in 1994. The accumulated trade deficit between January and April of this year fell 28 percent to $507 million, compared to $709 million in the first four months of 1995.
Pando added that copper accounted for 36 percent of Peru's mining exports, gold 22 percent, zinc 21 percent, lead nine percent, and silver six percent.
Pando said he expected by 2003 that production of copper would double, gold triple, zinc rise by 80 percent, lead 50 percent, iron 300 percent and silver 50 percent.
